key_insight: HandX provides a unified foundation—data, annotation, and evaluation—that enables scalable, high-fidelity generation of bimanual and finger-level human motion, capturing contact timing and inter-hand coordination that whole-body models miss.
problem_solved: Existing motion generation models and datasets lack high-resolution bimanual sequences and fine-grained annotations for finger articulation, contact events, and collaboration between hands, limiting realism in dexterous manipulation and interaction.
method: Assemble a large, high-fidelity bimanual motion dataset that preserves detailed finger trajectories and realistic inter-hand interactions.
Introduce fine-grained annotation schemas for contact timing, grasp types, and hand-to-hand/object relationships to supervise precise coordination.
Provide a training and evaluation pipeline (foundation model + metrics) that jointly models finger articulation, contact events, and bimanual coordination for generation and benchmarking.
impact: HandX enables practitioners to train and evaluate models that generate much more realistic hand and bimanual behaviors, improving applications in robotics, VR/AR, animation, and HCI where dexterous manipulation matters.
visual_elements: Dataset montage: side-by-side sequences showing high-fidelity hand/finger trajectories versus coarse whole-body outputs
Contact timeline: per-finger timeline graphic indicating contact onset, duration, and release for coordinated grasps
Coordination diagram: skeleton overlays of both hands showing synchronized trajectories and inter-hand distance/force heatmap
Pipeline flowchart: data → annotation → model → evaluation with metric icons (precision of contact, coordination score, realism)
paper_title: HandX: Scaling Bimanual Motion and Interaction Generation
paper_authors: Zimu Zhang, Yucheng Zhang, Xiyan Xu, Ziyin Wang, Sirui Xu
